name: Electric-Assisted Bicycle
description: A bicycle with two or three wheels, a saddle, fully operative pedals and an electric motor of no more than 750 watts, in one of three classes: pedal-assist to 20 mph, throttle-capable to 20 mph, or pedal-assist to 28 mph. Defined by Revised Code of Washington §46.04.169, as amended by ESSB 6110 (Chapter 159, Laws of 2026, effective June 11, 2026), and regulated by §46.61.710.

restrictions.rule: Class 1 assists only while pedaling and stops at 20 mph; Class 2 can propel the bike on its own but can't assist past 20 mph; Class 3 assists only while pedaling, stops at 28 mph and must have a speedometer
Two or three wheels, a saddle, fully operative pedals, and a motor with a power output of no more than 750 watts

Since June 11, 2026, anything capable of exceeding 20 mph on its motor alone, or designed or sold to be easily switched out of the e-bike limits by a switch, button, software setting or app, is not an e-bike; it falls under the motorcycle or moped rules instead

Manufacturers and distributors of new e-bikes must permanently affix a label in at least 9-point Arial stating its class, top assisted speed and motor wattage, and meet the CPSC's bicycle requirements
Must not be tampered with or modified to change its speed capability unless the label is replaced to match
Riders under 16 may not ride a Class 3
Has access to highways and may be parked to the same extent as a bicycle, and is otherwise subject to the same rules as a bicycle
Class 1 and Class 2 may ride on shared-use paths and any part of a highway designated for bicycles, but local jurisdictions and state agencies may restrict or regulate them on facilities they control
Class 3 may ride on facilities within or next to a highway, but not on a shared-use path unless the local jurisdiction allows it
A Class 3 may not ride on a sidewalk unless the sidewalk is the only way through as part of a bicycle or pedestrian path, or a local ordinance allows it
Not allowed on natural-surface trails designated nonmotorized unless the local authority or state agency that manages the trail allows it
No driver's license or registration required
